changesApplied.why: No foreign harness name is baked in any more.

changesApplied.before: loadMpdConfig({..., harness: "codex"}) at both call sites
changesApplied.why: codegraph's own settings now come from the block that belongs to this project.

changesApplied.why: Enumerations replaced by shape matching; the [mpd] layer is read from the RAW config before this strip runs (resolveMpdConfigView builds layers first, returns withoutControlKeys(config2) after the merge).

changesApplied.before: `[opencode]`, `[senpi]`, `[codex]` properties in MpdConfigProfileSchema, MpdConfigSchema, MpdConfigLayerSchema; plus the now-unreferenced MpdOpenHostHarnessConfigSchema / MpdTypedHarnessConfigSchema definitions
changesApplied.after: all foreign block properties and both harness-config schemas deleted; MpdControlBlockSchema = record(string, unknown) accepts the project block, wired as `[mpd]` in MpdConfigLayerSchema
changesApplied.why: Layer-level strict validation must still accept the owner block (measured necessity, see below) while rejecting genuinely unknown keys.
Captain ruling: never write a foreign product's schema URL into a DSH user's config.

changesApplied.before: carried [opencode], [codex], [senpi]/[upstream] blocks into the rewritten document
changesApplied.after: carries only the project's own keys (codegraph, …) and the migration history
changesApplied.why: The retargeted surface no longer corresponds to those blocks, and re-emitting a foreign block would re-plant it in the user's file.
Removes the OMO_CODEGRAPH_* / CODEX_CODEGRAPH_* reads mandated by the task; the project's own MPD_CODEGRAPH_* overrides keep working.

changesApplied.after: deleted (no reader in the artifact, no writer anywhere)

changesApplied.before: getCodexMpdConfig / codexCodegraphConfig / runCodexConfigMigration / runCodexStartupMigration / `mpd-codex: ` warning prefix / "not supported for harness codex"
changesApplied.after: getMpdConfig / projectCodegraphConfig / runMpdConfigMigration / runMpdStartupMigration / `mpd-config: ` / "not supported by this harness"
changesApplied.why: User-visible and internal vocabulary now matches the project.

deliberatelyNotRenamed.reason: FLOOR — persisted migration state (the user's `_migrations` marker, the journal migrationId, the backup-name fallback). It is now the ONLY codex token left in the artifact. t6's brand guard must carry it as an explicit allowlist entry with the data-compat reason.

Configs written by the previous release carry the foreign URL and a LAYER is rejected whole if the key is unknown (`readConfigSource` -> MpdConfigLayerSchema.safeParse). Dropping the key from the layer schema would silently discard a real user's codegraph settings on read. We stop WRITING it (B7/B8) and keep READING it.

retargetProof.probe: raw/probe.mjs (kept byte-identical to step-a/raw/probe.mjs; sha256 in the run records)
retargetProof.artifact_under_test: the landed artifact itself — no copies, no substitutions

falsifiablePair.b1_mpd_block_disables: [mpd].codegraph.enabled=false -> codegraph SUPPRESSED (stderr: 'CodeGraph MCP skipped: disabled by .mpd config. Set codegraph.enabled=true to enable it.')
falsifiablePair.b2_foreign_codex_block_inert: [codex].codegraph.enabled=false -> codegraph NOT suppressed (no disabled hint at all)
falsifiablePair.verdict: PASS — the block NAME is what decides whether codegraph is configurable, so the foreign block is genuinely inert and [mpd] is genuinely the owner block.

otherRuns.b3_legacy_schema_still_validates: a config carrying a foreign $schema URL is still accepted (migration executed, then the guard skipped as already-recorded)
otherRuns.b4_plain_migration_due: control — the migration writes (196 -> 253 bytes) and leaves a .bak sibling

orderVerification.claim: [mpd] is read from the RAW config BEFORE the generic strip and the strict parse
orderVerification.measured: b1 suppresses, which is only possible if harnessLayer read `[mpd]` out of the raw merged config; the same run shows the block absent from the resolved view (the written document carries no bracket key at all).

measuredSchemaNecessity.finding: The first retarget version removed the foreign block properties and added nothing, and BOTH b1 and b2 then failed to apply — because `readConfigSource` validates each file against MpdConfigLayerSchema and a rejected layer is dropped in full.
measuredSchemaNecessity.consequence: MpdControlBlockSchema + the `[mpd]` property are REQUIRED for the owner block to be readable at all; they are not decoration.

mcpSurface.how: the real packages/mpd-mcp-codegraph/launch.mjs driven over stdio with MCP JSON-RPC, sandbox HOME + sandbox project, MPD_CODEGRAPH_BIN pinned to a path-looking sentinel
mcpSurface.mode: DEGRADED — no codegraph binary in the sandbox, stderr: 'CodeGraph MCP skipped: codegraph binary not found. Install CodeGraph or set MPD_CODEGRAPH_BIN.' The surface stays alive in the degraded mode rather than dying.
